answers.topic: What questions should you not ask during a tarot reading
answers.question: What questions should you not ask during a tarot reading?
answers.fits: questions not to ask tarot reading
answers.text:
Skip anything where the answer would hand your decision to the cards, or where a wrong answer could hurt you.

Three kinds are worth avoiding. First, medical, legal and money questions: should I stop this medication, will I win the case, should I put my savings into this. A card cannot know those facts, and a reader who answers them confidently is guessing. Take those to a doctor, lawyer or financial adviser. Second, questions about a specific person's private thoughts, like what is he thinking right now. The cards only reflect your side of the story, so you get your own worry handed back. Third, yes or no questions about a fixed future, like will I get the job. They invite a verdict, and tarot is a poor verdict machine.

Ask instead what you should consider, what you are not seeing, or what would help this week. A question that starts with how or what usually gives you something you can act on. If a reader pushes you toward fear or tells you to pay more to remove a curse, leave.

answers.topic: What are good questions to ask Tarot cards
answers.question: What are good questions to ask Tarot cards?
answers.fits: good questions to ask tarot cards
answers.text:
The good ones are open, about you, and about the next step rather than a fixed outcome.

Some that work well: What do I need to understand about this situation right now? What am I avoiding looking at? What would help me make this decision with a clearer head? What is one thing I can change this week? How can I approach this conversation honestly?

What makes them work is that every card in the spread, even a hard one like the Tower or the Moon reversed, gives you something to think about instead of a yes or no to accept. Compare that with will he text me back, which the cards cannot know and which only leaves you more anxious.

One practical tip: write the question down before you shuffle, in one sentence. If you cannot write it plainly, the question is not ready yet, and working that out is often most of the value. Tarot is a reflection tool. For health, money or legal questions, talk to a qualified professional.

answers.topic: tarot reading same question every day
answers.question: Will it be inaccurate if you get a tarot reading on the same question done every single day?
answers.text:
It will not be more or less accurate. It will usually get less useful.

Each shuffle is a fresh draw, so asking the same question daily gives you different cards each time. If you treat the cards as predictions, that looks like a contradiction and creates anxiety. If you treat them as prompts for reflection, it is simply seven different angles on one situation, which can be useful for a week and then stops adding anything.

The pattern to watch for is asking again because you did not like the first answer. That is the moment tarot stops helping and starts feeding the worry.

A better routine: ask once, write down what the cards made you think, act on one small thing, and wait a few weeks before asking again. If a different card appeared each day for the same worry, look for the theme across them, not the single card. Tarot is for reflection and cannot predict a fixed outcome.

answers.question: For those who read tarot, do you read with reversals? Why or why not?
answers.text:
I read with reversals, but only in a light way.

A reversed card is not a bad card. In my readings it usually means the energy is blocked, delayed or turned inward. Reversed Ten of Swords, for example, often reads as the worst being over and you not yet admitting it. Reversed Sun is still a warm card, just one where the good news is hard to enjoy right now.

The practical reason: reversals add nuance to a three card spread without needing a bigger spread. The practical risk: beginners who also memorize 78 upright meanings get overloaded and stop trusting what they see.

If you are new, learn the upright meanings first for a month, then add reversals. If you never use them, you lose nothing. Plenty of good readers skip them. Pick the method you will use consistently, and note your results in a journal so you can see what works for you.
